summary: The production wrapper previously hid both procedural upper arms while retaining the PFD and assembled MetaHuman body, leaving a narrow or disconnected transition from the vest to the arms. Visible Shoulders V1 adds two project-owned splash-jacket upper sleeves. Each sleeve starts at the authoritative solved shoulder, follows the live shoulder-to-elbow segment, remains elongated in the shortest tested gameplay pose, and restores a rounded upper-body silhouette without adding flotation shoulder pads to the PFD.

root_cause.production_visibility_gap: SetProceduralVisualVisible(false) retained torso, PFD, waist, boots, helmet and paddle overlays but hid both procedural upper arms; the assembled body did not provide a reliable visible deltoid bridge outside the fitted PFD.
root_cause.rejected_cap_iterations: Three isolated shoulder-cap candidates were rejected because closed ellipsoids and short capsules read as rigid balls or vest shoulder pads.
root_cause.retained_shape: A continuous shoulder-to-elbow garment sleeve with a 5.2 cm reference radius; live pose length remains authoritative and no shoulder point is invented.

renderer_evidence.technical_verdict: pass: guide and broadest-body front, profile and rear views retain rounded body shoulders behind an unpadded PFD
renderer_evidence.photoreal_verdict: fail pending named review or replacement of the still-simplified procedural sleeve anatomy, seams, deformation and wet material response

validation.focused_python: 36/36 production-character, safety-gear, and flexible-raft source contracts passed
validation.m5: 5/5 passed renderer-enabled, including live shoulder visibility and anchor assertions (M9V570VisibleShouldersM5Renderer)
validation.failed_diagnostic: M9V569VisibleShouldersM5Renderer was rejected because its turntable-oriented 6.4 cm half-length floor did not admit the valid 5.87 cm live rescue sleeve; it is not retained as passing evidence.

accepted: Both production shoulders now have a visible, pose-matched garment bridge from the solved shoulder to the assembled arm.
All five roster identities meet the radius, elongated-shape and 0.25 cm joint-anchor contracts.
The PFD still has zero flotation shoulder pads; only its existing narrow webbing crosses the shoulders.
No animation, body mass, collision, raft, water, rescue or gameplay-force authority changed.
rejected_or_open: Large cyan deltoid ellipsoids were rejected because they read as rigid protective pads.
Reduced dark ellipsoids were rejected because they still floated as disconnected balls.
Short shoulder capsules were rejected because the shortest pose clamped them into spheres.
The retained procedural garment sleeves remain visibly synthetic and do not satisfy final photoreal character-art acceptance.
No named character-art reviewer or qualified guide has approved these captures for release media.
open_gates: A named character-art reviewer must approve or replace the sleeve anatomy, torso integration, deformation, seams and wet-material response.
A qualified whitewater guide must approve shoulder range of motion and paddle-stroke biomechanics in motion.
M9 remains blocked by all wider human, platform, signing, media, clean-build, performance and promotion gates.
